text.p: Starter Corp said Thursday it expects results for the balance of the year will be "substantially" below last year's levels, and it is disappointed 1997 will not be a year of financial improvement.

The company said, however, it is confident Starter will end the year better positioned for growth in 1998. It said it is foused on improving its quick response programs and on continuing the development of its retail partnerships.
In the second quarter, the company said two factors hurt its sales.
It said the comparison with last year's sales figures was "difficult" because of strong Olympic sales last year.
It also said a challenging retail market in general hurt its sales figures this year.
In addition, the company said the first-time inclusion of expenses associated with operations at Starter Galt and Starter Benelux affected its results in the quarter.
The company reported a loss per share for the quarter of $0.17 compared to a loss per share of $0.12.
It reported sales of $58.3 million compared to $62.8 million.
